about: The machine-readable H3 prompt contract. Read this before auditing, changing, or adding a prompt: it is the one place that states what the output must look like per mode, what vocabulary is legal, what blocks each system prompt carries and in what order, and which guide line each of those comes from. test/contract.test.ts binds every field here to the implementation, so a disagreement is a build failure rather than a stale document.
notWrittenByHand: Nothing here is generated. It is written independently of the code on purpose -- a spec derived from the implementation cannot contradict it, and therefore cannot catch it being wrong.

sources.title: Video Prompt Writing Guide (T2VA / I2VA / FL2VA / L2VA)
sources.note: The hash is checked. A guide revision should be a deliberate, visible event: replace the file, update the hash, and let the golden tests report everything the revision changed.

sources.title: Full-Reference Mode Rewrite Output Format Guide

I2VA.alignment: For the target video, at 0.00 seconds into the target video, <Picture 1> (from [Shot 1]) is fully referenced.

FL2VA.alignment: How the reference pictures align with the target video — Picture 1 (from Shot 1) aligns with the 0.00-second mark of the target video; Picture 2 (from Shot {N}) aligns with the {S.SS}-second mark of the target video.
FL2VA.alignmentNote: Bare. This one line uses Picture 1 and Shot 1 without angle or square brackets, unlike every other citation in the format. The guide's own worked example does, and a fixture proves it.

L2VA.alignment: How the reference pictures align with the target video — <Picture 1> (from [Shot {N}]) aligns with the {S.SS}-second mark of the target video.

shotHeader.note: The cut phrasing itself is prose inside the beat, not part of the header. The guide asks for it as natural language in the sentence.

specialCuts.note: Only when the user explicitly asks.

sceneTrans.note: Both sides of a line that crosses a cut.

cutoff.note: Speech truncated by the end of the video; final beat only.

voiceoverPhrase.note: Exact phrase, followed by a statement that the lips remain closed.

speakerIds.note: Numbered by the order of actual vocal events; never renumbered; never written in retention_analysis (ref 5.4).

onScreenText.quoting: English double quotation marks, verbatim, untranslated

mediaKinds.note: House partition of reference assets. Neither guide enumerates media kinds; it exists so a slot can be typed.

slotCeilings.note: Not in either guide -- neither states any limit on reference assets. A platform limit carried without a guide citation.

exemptions: video editing: the description scales with the complexity of the source video and is not held to this range
dialogue-dense material: fitting the complete spoken timeline outranks the count
refDetailWords.note: The scope is part of the rule. Stating the bare range overstates the guide, which is how the planner came to apply it to video-editing jobs.

planner.note: Blocks are joined in this order. Anything marked conditional is absent when its input is absent. Adding a block means adding it here first; the conformance test fails otherwise.

blocks.heading: # Recognisable people
blocks.note: Not in either guide. From the Sora prompt architecture and the original engine's own fragment. Carve-out: dialogue text and on-screen text are reproduced verbatim regardless.

blocks.heading: # Active mode:
blocks.note: One per mode; the heading carries the mode name.

blocks.heading: # Style direction
blocks.note: From CreativeModeRecord.selection. Absent when no pack resolves.

blocks.heading: # Glitch marks
blocks.note: From CreativeModeRecord.glitch. The planner appends a mode-specific affordance note; the patch prompt does not, because it has no mode.

blocks.heading: # Supplied facts
blocks.note: Last on purpose, so the facts have the final word.

patch.parity: Both prompts derive the style and glitch blocks from the same record through the same function, so an edit cannot drift from what the document was written under. test/creative-integration.test.ts asserts the derived text is identical on both sides.

invariants.statement: The planner writes the sentences; the serializer assembles structure around them and never expands an enum into a sentence.
invariants.enforcedBy: review, and the absence of any enum-to-prose path in src/core/serialize

invariants.statement: serialize(doc, ctx) is total and deterministic. Nothing hand-edits prompt text.
src/core has no React, DOM, network, SDK or idb.
A diagnostic means the document is provably malformed. There is no warning severity.
Every diagnostic code has a fixture that makes it fire.
A creative selection and a wildcard roll travel as records; their text is derived at the point of use.
The five golden fixtures are the guides' worked examples, byte for byte.
Stored ids this build does not know resolve to nothing rather than failing to load.

diagnostics.note: Every code the validator can emit, with what makes it legitimate. Guide-derived codes cite a section; house codes say so. test/validate.test.ts proves each one can fire; the conformance test proves this list matches the codes the rules actually emit.

codes.NO_SHOTS: house: a document with no shots renders nothing
codes.DURATION_NOT_POSITIVE: house: duration drives every derived timestamp
codes.SHOT_1_HAS_TIMESTAMP: base 4.2: the first shot carries no timestamp
codes.CUT_OUTSIDE_DURATION: base 4.2: cuts fall within the video duration
codes.CUT_STYLE_NOT_IN_PROSE: base 4.2: the cut phrasing is one of five exact strings, and the annotation must be the one the prose uses
codes.SHOT_NO_BEATS: house: a shot with no prose renders an empty header
codes.FRAME_ROLE_ON_NON_IMAGE: ref 2.2: only images are frame anchors
codes.SLOT_NO_ROLES: house: a slot with no role has no label kind
codes.SLOT_ORDER_NOT_CONTIGUOUS: house: connection order drives label ordinals
codes.SPEAKER_ORDER_WRONG: base 4.4: ids follow the order of actual vocal events
codes.SPEAKER_REF_MISSING_IN_PROSE: base 4.4: the id is written in the prose
codes.DIALOGUE_PLACEHOLDER_ORPHAN: house: a splice point with nothing to splice
codes.DIALOGUE_BAD_TERMINAL: ref 5.4: complete statements end . ? or ! -- scoped to dialogue the user did not supply, since base 4.4 preserves supplied punctuation verbatim
codes.DIALOGUE_DECORATIVE_PUNCT: ref 5.4: no repeated or decorative punctuation -- same scope, and for the same reason
codes.VOICEOVER_PHRASE_MISSING: base 4.4: the exact phrase. The lips-closed clause the same section requires is a prompt instruction, not a check: the guide mandates the statement rather than a wording, so no allowlist can prove its absence
codes.SCENETRANS_UNPAIRED: base 4.4: both sides of a line crossing a cut
codes.CUTOFF_NOT_AT_END: base 4.4: truncation by the end of the video
codes.REF_TASK_TYPE_DUPLICATE: ref 3: do not repeat a type
codes.REF_SUMMARY_NEW_LABEL: ref 3: no new labels in the summary
codes.REF_LABEL_UNDEFINED: ref 2: a cited label is defined
codes.REF_RETENTION_MISSING: ref 4: one line per reference label
codes.REF_RETENTION_MARKER_WRONG_CLASS: ref 4.1 and 4.2: visual and audio markers are different sets
codes.REF_SPEAKER_IN_RETENTION: ref 5.4: do not write (Sx) in retention_analysis

notInTheGuides.note: Everything the compiler does that no guide asks for. An audit should be able to tell contract from house style at a glance.

items.why: Naming a public figure pulls the frame toward a likeness. From the Sora prompt architecture.
Style direction injected into the planner prompt. Never reaches the serializer.
Anomalous tokenizer strings placed as visible on-screen text. Uses the guide's on-screen text rule rather than a new one.
Content substitution on the idea, before anything is planned. Never touches beat prose or serialized output.
17k+5 at 24fps is a workflow fact, not a guide rule.
2.5 words per second is an estimate, supplied to the planner as advice.
MS_PER_BEAT, one dominant beat per 2.5 seconds. House judgement. Neither guide contains a density rule, and the comment here attributed one to the guide until an outside audit searched for it.
SLOT_CEILINGS, 9 images / 3 videos / 3 audio. Neither guide states any limit on reference assets; marked house in the vocabulary block as well.
